text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The eight victims of the Pala bus collision were burried yesterday. Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi attended the ceremony.

- Three MPs protested against the draft budget for 1997 as being introduced illegally since the draft did not include the amendments to laws which it requires. The opposition was highly critical of the draft budget.
- Interior Minister Mart Raesk threatened to resign unless the interior ministry budget is increased.
- The draft law on increased fuel excise was debated in parliament. Finance Minister Mart Opmann was unable to defend the draft convincingly, the newspaper says.
- The ruling coalition discussed the strains within the cabinet and the Reform Party intends to reconsider its position after the local elections, which take place this weekend.
- The finance ministry has prepared the draft law on car tax, to be imposed on all motor vehicles.

- A conference on poverty took place yesterday: a World Bank report claims 130,000 Estonian inhabitants (nearly 10 percent) lived in poverty at the end of 1995. Official subsistence minimum is 390 kroons a month but the minimum food basket cost is estimated at 800 kroons a month.
- Border guard fears that a reduced budget for 1997 will halt its development and complicate transition to professional personnel, director Tarmo Kduts said.

- Estonian firms spend little on charity, a study revealed; a quarter do not donate for charities and 50 percent give less than 50,000 kroons per year. Business leaders are more willing to donate. The most popular recipients are sports, welfare and education.
- The ESOIL court cases obstructing the privatisation of the oil firm have been settled and the solution is expected within a week.
- The justice ministry prepared a law on the regulation of private enterprise, which will require all activities to be licensed, business associations oppose the plan.
